title: In Python, 'add 24 hours' and 'add 1 day' land on the same wall-clock minute across a DST jump
assumption: Adding a timedelta of 24 hours to a timezone-aware datetime moves it forward by exactly 24 real hours, the same way adding 1 day does if you just mean 'tomorrow'.

input.description: A 'remind me in 24 hours' feature, or a billing-cycle / subscription renewal computed by adding a fixed duration to a timestamp, run across the March DST change.

what_goes_wrong: A 'remind me in exactly 24 hours' feature built on Python's aware-datetime arithmetic fires at the same wall-clock minute as 'remind me tomorrow', not 24 real hours later -- on the spring-forward day the two features that were supposed to differ by design turn out identical, and neither one is actually 24 elapsed hours.
why: CPython's datetime arithmetic for aware datetimes adds the timedelta to the naive (wall-clock) fields first, then reinterprets the result in the same zone -- it does not convert to UTC, add, and convert back. So timedelta(hours=24) and timedelta(days=1) both just add to the naive calendar fields and land on the same wall-clock time, 2024-03-10 12:00, even though only 23 real hours separate the two instants because of the lost hour. Subtraction follows the same rule: subtracting two datetimes that share a tzinfo returns the wall-clock difference (1 day here, not the 23 real hours); Python only goes through UTC when the operands have different tzinfo objects. JavaScript's Date stores a UTC millisecond count, so adding 24*3600*1000 to getTime() is 24 real elapsed hours and renders as 13:00, not 12:00, in the DST-affected zone (the repro). JavaScript also has wall-clock arithmetic, but only in the host's local zone and only through the local setters: in a process running in America/New_York, both setDate(getDate() + 1) and setHours(getHours() + 24) land on 12:00 the next day, 23 real hours later, just like Python.
affects: javascript (Date local-time setters such as setHours/setDate)

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

tz = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
start = datetime(2024, 3, 9, 12, 0, tzinfo=tz)
plus_24h = start + timedelta(hours=24)
plus_1day = start + timedelta(days=1)
print("start:", start, "| +24h:", plus_24h, "| +1day:", plus_1day)
print("+24h == +1day (same wall clock):", plus_24h == plus_1day)
print("+24h in UTC:", plus_24h.astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC")))
print("real elapsed hours:", (plus_24h.astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC")) - start.astimezone(ZoneInfo("UTC"))).total_seconds() / 3600)

repros.expected_output:
start local: 03/09/2024, 12:00
start + 24 real hours, local: 03/10/2024, 13:00

fix: Decide explicitly whether you mean 'N real hours of elapsed time' (convert to UTC, add, convert back -- or just do the arithmetic in UTC) or 'the same wall-clock time N calendar days later' (use calendar-aware addition that is documented to do that, e.g. `dateutil.relativedelta`). Never assume Python's aware `timedelta` arithmetic gives you the first one; it gives you something closer to the second.
